commentBody:
Now that was a Friday!
Thanks, Katie Hoody.
A very nice puzzle, but more at a Saturday level of trickiness than a Friday one IMO.  But a great puzzle either way!
30A is genius.

That was one terrific Friday puzzle!  It was quite the challenge. At no point did I feel completely stalled, but had to circulate all over the puzzle multiple times in order to eventually make progress. The kind of puzzle that leaves me with a sense of accomplishment when it is finally solved.

Nice tough Friday with some excellent clues, especially the one for TANLINES.  I struggled in the NW because I stubbornly held on to EDIE Sedgwick and tried whip instead of WHUP and olden instead of THOSE.  I’m guessing that LUXURYTAX will perplex the non sports fanatics among us, but it was catnip for me and my biggest foothold in my first pass.

Wow, what a gift to a LOGOMANIAc to see Katie Hoody’s byline. This was just one gem of a clue and entry after another. There are some people who just have a genius for constructing and Katie is definitely one of those.

Where to start?
Peaty and Oatie—thanks for making Sonja HENIE a gimme. I can’t say why but you know.

Two Cincinnati call outs—the OHIO river and yes I am counting Jimmy Buffett. For some reason he was a Cincinnati fan favorite, played here every single summer, what a fun performer who always made you smile.

Proud to say I almost got BBQ right off the bat. I had RIB joint but I still count that as a win.

I’m ASHAMED to admit I don’t know all my plagues in order, despite 64 plus Seders; but I got the plural misdirection of GRANT pretty quickly and that gave me the G.

Some wonderful misdirects, my favorites were TANLINES and SEXT—but all the clues just felt original and sparkling. I think this should be a great example of Friday level of difficulty . It didn’t take me so long—I wouldn’t call it a Saturday—but there were few gimmes, I always felt engaged and challenged, and I had a ton of Aha moments (is the plural of Aha AHI?) and smiles and SLY winks.

Is Katie Hoodie treading into Robyn Weintraub territory? I think so. I can’t think of a more consistently brilliant themeless constructor in the Times lately.
Tough but good. Really enjoyed this one.

I'm ashamed that the USTA/HARTE crossing was my last square. I thought of court of law, basketball courts, even volleyball courts, but not the kind of court I watch about 40 weeks a year and the organization I patronize nonstop for three weeks every year
I'm quite certain I am not the only Taskmaster fan here. Did anyone else hear Kumail Nanjiani in their head for 7D? (What?!) https://youtube.com/shorts/YUB9YiuJVHs

Outstanding puzzle!  Loved the clues for 30A (FLATMATE) and 38A (TAN LINES), and 29D (SLANT RHYME) was a stellar entry (though perhaps clueing it by an example would have made it a bit more difficult).

I was tripped up at the start by 5D ("Edie" instead of "KYRA") and 31D ("logorrhea" instead of LOGOMANIA).

Whenever I see Katie's name in the byline, I know I'm in for a creative, clever,  and challenging puzzle.
Took me about 60% longer than my Friday average but absolutely loved the challenge - and I enjoyed reading about Uncle Tim - such great memories!
Bookmarking this for POY. Lewis is going to have to expand his favorite clues this week, I think, to accommodate the excellent clues in this puzzle alone. Bravo, Katie!

Why is the Friday crossword the "opening to our solving weekend"? Is it a very long-standing thing? I mean it's still Thursday evening...
Just a noob question, sorry!

More than double my average Friday time, but no complaints!  This was outstanding.  Every nasty clue that I misinterpreted initially (an embarrassingly large number) turned out to be fair and gettable.

Also, my very partial and lame excuse is that I was trying to watch the Bears-Patriots game while solving.  That does slow you down.

But sometimes you just have to tip your hat to the constructor.  Awesome puzzle!
Delightfully chewy for a Friday! I sweated over this one for sure, but it was always just frustrating enough.
Great puzzle-- thank you Katie Hoody!  A fun solve  with fresh and nicely tricky clues.   And even more, the lovely write-up about  Uncle Tim ...

Hoo boy another toughie! 12 minutes over par but oh so satisfactory when that gold star came up.

Great puzzle. Way to go!
I know it’s going to be a fun puzzle when I see Katie’s name. Superb clues as always!

A terrific puzzle, topped off with a touching ode to Uncle Tim. Amazing, Katie. Respect. I didn’t think I'd get to fill in much of the grid, but very slowly and meticulously, thinking and rethinking what seemed like every other entry, dissecting and pondering over almost every clue, it came together in what felt like a miracle. What an outstanding romp that was! But— for all that I did end up knowing or deducing, it was WHUP/USTA that did me in. I knew it was a sports court, but not which one. And I thought it was spelled WHooP, so I went with WHiP. And that wasn’t all. I was completely onomatopoeia challenged today. I went with BOINg before correcting it to BOINK to make DISKS work. Welk, that BOINg was enough for me to take a break and go listen to some Oingo BOINgo... https://youtu.be/EJGykmmBjP4?is=bVN33AGRx2SXZDl6 Maybe for Oingo Boingo it was "Just Another Day," but not for this here puzzler. With a Hoody byline, it was one heck of a special day. Thank you, Katie!

Someone took my metronome. Now I'm ticked!

(I'll have to control my tempo.)

Hoody's dialed up the difficulty and eased off the elegance just a bit with this Friday.  

Feels like a Weintraub if she were setting in order to COOLOFF after an argument with an editor but is still fuming a bit and has to let the residual spleen out on someone - us.

Not complaining a bit.

Splenically clever misdirection beats dad puns any day.

Put me through my paces in all the good ways.
A near double pangram, except no v or z. Was this a goal that slipped away?  Still fine, challenging puzzle. Got Kyra from crosses.

I got nothing other than, like everyone here, thought it was sensational.

I mean, just do it...it's as obvious as the sky is blue, grass is green, and The Constitution is the Law of the land.  Life would be unbearable were these not true.

This was the most wonderfully bewildering assortment of straightforward clues and clues which looked *exactly* like ones that would end with a "?" had our editors any mercy.

So when I was looking for a curve ball and got a fast ball, and visa versa.

I was deep, deep into give-up territory, flyspecking, unsure of about a half dozen places but without anything better to try.

Then, finally.  boom...it's Amanda BYNES, not BYNEr.  And that changes that weird thingy used in Othello, into a little more reasonable DISgS, still ugly...but wait BOINg and BOINK are the same things that that makes DISKS and...

...another major meltdown avoided.
Absolutely brilliant.

I enjoyed the clever cluing, but am surprised to not see more complaining about that NW bit.  WHUP (instead of the equally fitting WHiP) and HORNE crossing USTA nearly did me in. Not because of the tennis misdirect (I assumed court would be a sports reference) but just because a 4 letter acronym could conceivably be anything.

Overall I powered through, and actually had no problem sussing out the delightful puns like FLATMATE. But some of the other, seemingly straightforward cluing was just so far from my wavelength!

What a richly satisfying way to end the week.  Clues that led you astray, crosses that made you look again, then flee to another block of the puzzle to lick your wounds and take another try a a fill that was "right" but wrong (Well, if it isn't near RHYMEs. then what is it??), whirling around the puzzle like you were at a Saturday night dance with one gorgeous partner after another.

Katie Hoody, you gave us a goody.  Thank you!

As a non-US solver I found that tough! Quite proud to have managed to solve it only slightly below my average Friday time.

My standout today was flatmates, but I think it may have just been schadenfreude knowing that some US solvers might get a taste of my struggle 🤣🤣🤣.

All in all, I loved the difficulty level and liked the puzzle.

As a small man who lives on the subway i must register my umbrage at the inclusion of METRONOME in today’s puzzle. I humbly appeal to all readers to boycott the NYT until it withdraws this offensive slur. I really thought we had moved beyond this kind of thing, but alas it seems not. And don’t think i didn’t notice the clue about getting a leg up!



(Well, someone had to hate today’s puzzle, didn’t they? I thought I’d try to restore some balance!)

So... I thought Buffet was all Florida, they wear leis? Ok then.

Also, just a pet peeve, but looking at the USA from outside, the Dems aren't really very left at all.

The constructor's notes in the Wordplay column about her uncle's poetry remind me of a song my mother used to sing to me. It's a not-so-nice take on Cornell's alma mater. The original: "Far above Cayuga's waters, With its waves of blue, Stands our noble Alma Mater, Glorious to view." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rJxV4Lu4gKM And the 29D [Poetic device with inexact sound-alikes] SLANGRHYME version: "Far above Cayuga's waters There's an awful smell Some say it's Cayuga's waters Some say it's ........" Well, Cayuga is one of the beautiful Finger Lakes (in Ithaca), but 9A [One of the fam] MOMMA's version didn't exactly make me look forward to going to college....
Dang!

The perfect Friday with some wonderfully clever cluing!! I started out with barely anything on the first pass, but then it all fell into place so neatly. Lotsa fun wordplay, no naticks... Absolutely loved it ❤️

my comments are fresh from solving not reading the always wonderful article in support or comments from others:  a classic Friday Katie nothing but superlatives about your effort - it made me really have to think on your wavelength plus the clues and answers are 'al dente' JUST RIGHT.  bravo!

I found the puzzle insaneIy difficult but I managed to solve it on my own. It took everything I had (and nearly 50 minutes), and I'm very proud of my success. I swear, if I see somebody saying this was too easy, I'll think less of them 🤣

I enjoyed, nay - loved! - how the difficulty was due to misdirection rather than an overreliance on esoterica - there was personally arcane trivia, of course (MARYJANES, for example - seeing such a long and completely unknown entry was daunting!) but the beauty of the grid was that I could deal with (almost) all of it using my wit rather than factual knowledge. I needed to guess just one square, at my only naticky crossing of HAR_E and US_A - I assumed the T in USTA stood for tennis.

This was one of the hardest Fridays I have ever solved, and one of the most enjoyable, too.

I loved this oodles and oodles of miniature poodles.

Based on the last two weeks, Friday may be replacing Thursday as my favorite puzzle day. (I got so annoyed at yesterday’s, I actually hit Reveal Puzzle just to be done with it,)

This, on the other hand, was a delight. And couldn’t we all use an Uncle Tim in our lives.  Thanks, Katie.

Great puzzle, with some really fun clues. I have to take exception with one, however. While the spelling of onomatopoeia may be subjective sometimes, the cartoon bouncing sound is generally BOING; BOINK is the sound of a hit.

I've got to join in on the love fest; impossible not to express my appreciation post-solve. That was the most fun I've had wrestling with a puzzle in a long time. Just perfect.

Everyone else has articulated what was so wonderful about it so I will leave it at that. 

Top 5 favorite constructor notes, also. Just an amazing start to the day!

Thanks so much, Katie!
Tough but fun clues.
SHEESH what a puzzle!! Had me absolutely bamboozled and backwards for first 30 mins. Lovely Friday!!

Nice Friday puzzle!

Names are often tough for me, so I was happy to able able to put in edie at 5 D with no crosses.  That definitely cost me time in the NW.

I had show OFF instead of COOL OFF for [Count to ten, perhaps] and thought that was an uncharitable way to describe what children do.  I mean, they're just kids, Katie, give them a break!  

Great clues all around.  There's a reason Katie Hoody's name always pops up in my POY list.
Formidable Friday.  Took 17% longer than average.  Don't know what else to say. It was hard and I got it done.

It’s been a tough week for me crossword wise. All of them morasses of dense, indecipherable clueing and a slew of TIL answers. Today was no exception…in the best way possible. Seeing Ms Hoody’s name I knew I was in for a challenging but enjoyable time. She didn’t disappoint. I’m relieved to read that some others shared my experience of far too much white space after the first couple of passes, then slowly filling them in, with a few aha moments. I had no idea about the cartoon shoes, but once I had M and J the name came easily. I just hadn’t known where the name came from originally.

My only real natick was the crossing of 2 and 14D with 18A. WHUP a completely unknown word, I’d gone with WHiP, then WHoP. 18A still means nothing to me but ok. I suppose I should know the character’s name; the author came from my home town, where she also based her novel. Try as I might I could never get into her writing; far too melodramatic for my taste.

Once completed I went back through the clues, chuckling at the misdirects. Loved the clue for FLATMATE, THINK BIG to pick out two.

Thank you Ms Hoody, you’ve restored my faith in the crossword, it has been a tad tested this week.

Your notes on Uncle Tim brought a tear to my eye. It was Uncle David for me; a wonderful man who gave me so many lovely memories, from teaching me to foxtrot to hilarious shopping expeditions. He passed his joy to my kids. Gone now but never forgotten.

A rhyme that slants?
No chance.


Gotta boink.
Another tough but fair one this week. Would’ve been a lot easier if I hadn’t hung on to SPOONERISM over SLANTRHYME and PINTOBEAN over GREENBEAN.

What a great puzzle! Took me 27% longer than my average, but I enjoyed every chewy minute of it. I nearly lost it trying to search all the old trunks in the dusty attic of my mind to remember MARYJANES; when I did it opened up that whole side for me. In addition to the great misdirections, the almost total lack of fill made every section a little victory. Thanks Katie, I knew it would be a good one when I saw your name, and you outdid yourself.
Oh, melt-my-heart constructor notes…

Wow. Two days in a row I was wondering if I would solve it as I rocketed past my daily average. Appropriately challenging and then some.

What has it been, forty years? Fifty? I still think of it as the USLTA, although I don't remember exactly when they dropped the L. It was still the first one I got today.

Nice reminder at 23A of Click and Clack and their frequent statement of amazement: "Sonia HENIE's tutu!"

And 44A, a callback to when the Grammys were still Tin Pan Alley's Revenge.

Was this intentional? Everything is, right? I enjoyed seeing RON Chernow so close not to Hamilton, but another subject of one of his biographies, GRANT. I was reading it on my Kindle, so as the weeks would go by I could report to my wife that even after many hours of reading I might have advanced only three or four percent. Totally worth reading, even if it never inspires a musical.

Thanks for the great lead-in to the weeend!

So enjoyed solving this puzzle today. I felt the AFTERGLOW after completion. I hade flat rate , though it didn't make sense, before flat mate, which made me smile. Loved the positive "buzz"
of the comments today. And so appreciated Katie sharing her Uncle Tim with us this morning!

It's so good to read so many upbeat and positive comments today. 
Weirdly, I found some clues easier - eg HORSE RACE, but stumbled again over the names - all of them. 

Never heard of Jimmy Buffet, though I do know of Warren. (Parrotheads?  Coral Reefer Band?) Bees' nest didn't work, and wasps' nest was too long .... 

At UK elections there are always cute photos in the papers of the dogs waiting outside polling stations ... so I thought dog not DEM!

I echo the positive comments already posted.

A classic Friday puzzle from Ms Hoody, where at first there seemed to be no hope until gradually my puzzle brain kicked into gear.  
My biggest problems ended up being in the Northeast, where I had Irk instead of ADO for bother, and I was convinced that Jefferson's most beautiful river was the ArnO. Hey, he could have nipped down to Florence during his years in Paris. Too much of  A Room With a View yesterday for me, I guess.
And I also had no idea about the Marvel person, though eventually the name made total sense from the clue.
No one's complained about Ms HENIE, yet, that I've noticed. The crosses must be kind. I only got her because relatives older than me would reference her and  she would be trotted out during Winter Olympics coverage on occasion. 
Thanks again, Katie.

From the high of seeing Katie’s name atop the grid to the low of initial stuckness and desperately foraging for footholds anywhere, to the thrill of the big breakthrough (METRONOME) yielding a flood of success, only to be repelled again and again by an impervious area, until finally I let go of an answer I was committed to, which opened the crack that let the light in…

That is, drama in the box, the best kind, a Hoody journey.

Bolstered by uncovering beauty – ACCESSORY, AFTERGLOW, BOINK, THINK BIG, COOL OFF, FOOLED YOU, TAN LINES.  Even beauty in the black box design that looks like a pinwheel in motion (not to mention yielding 18 longs).  

Icing being the rare-in-crosswords five-letter semordnilap (PEELS), and the shake-my-head-in-awe clue – [Areas between areas with different amounts of coverage] for TAN LINES.

Eleven puzzles into the Times, and, in my mind, you are already a legend, Katie.  I can’t wait for the dozenth.  Thank you for a splendid journey!
This has been a work week full of worthy puzzles.  Xwstats.com calls Monday's and Wednesday's puzzles Hard, and Tuesday's, Thursday's and Friday's Very Hard.  A good challenge for serious solvers.

Can we please just get a normal puzzle for once? This is a jumbled mess. The misdirects are beyond awful and witless. Random trivia serves no purpose (usta/harte - nice Natick). Just publish a book of riddles if that's what floats your boat. Nothing but awful and poorly edited construction lately. Four in a row of some of the worst puzzles i have ever done. Good grief man!
‘Twas a winner winner chicken dinner!

Katie Hoody has fast become a crowd pleaser with a growing list of great puzzles and collaborations. IMHO today’s puzzle not only confirms her star status but elevates it. It’s rare to see this tough crowd feeling a warm, satisfying AFTERGLOW on Friday (Robyn Weintraub excepted). Thanks, Katie!

Sorry to see so much negative commentary for yesterday’s puzzle. It took me too long to see the trick, but I done did it. I thought it was a pretty clever twist.
This puzzle was the most fun so far this year.

Rather than marching throught the acrosses and then the downs I like to solve in blocks, guessing at answers but not writing them down and trying to see how the grid fits together.  This often results in partial answers (MATE, RACE) and it is a blast when a section comes together.  

Also notable with today's gem is how it seemed inscrutable at first but the reaction to the finished grid is, "Of course! Why was that so hard?!"

This has indeed been a good week for serious solvers.  Many thanks.

What a week this has been - some very hard puzzles - I had to look up to get round a couple of the names - evidently I have a blank spot when it comes to H names !!  I hope tomorrows doesn’t follow with the hardest Saturday of all time.
Boink?? Isn’t it BOING?? Boink seems to be something else entirely

I vote Katie Hoody for best constructor notes ever. 

And just in case I get jammed up with a one-sentence post, I loved the puzzle, too. It was a delightful struggle.
I struggled heaps and heaps of Halloween Peeps!

May we all give thanks to the Uncle Tim in our lives, and with help be that person to someone else. 

Also, that was a great puzzle!  Thank you Ms. Hoodie.
Outstanding. Great clueing.

Since the gift of this clever puzzle is already being so rightly celebrated, I’ll just add this to the cheery chorus: If you’d like to fix the order of the Ten Plagues in your memory for future 46Aish clues, you could do worse than turn to Handel's oratorio Israel in Egypt. Here’s the movement “Their land brought forth FROGS,” with its perky, frog-hoppy air: https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=Z3WIGbzovmo&ra=m (No METRONOME in sight, but the pesky amphibians are leaping right on time. BOINK.)
Today is my birthday :)
A thoroughly enjoyable puzzle. Quite difficult, but not a slog in any way. Persistence rewarded!
Another excellent Hoody puzzle! Thanks, from a big fan
My favorite thing about today's crossword is the constructor notes. They made me feel all warm and fuzzy, which helped ease the sting of how long it took me to finally complete this puzzle.
I'm more of a BOING guy for a "bouncing sound" and BOINK the sound made when a superhero is inclined to WHUP NITRO.
Just what a Friday is supposed to provide. Thanks.

Wow, I can't believe I managed to finish this puzzle!!
Every clue (well, almost every) was crafted to be as fiendish and obscure as could possibly be achieved, and one was forced to winkle out multiple meanings.
I was reduced to thinking things like, "Maybe Bob DYLAN was called 'Bobby' when he was a complete unknown..."
And then there were still puzzles like MAMMA MOMMY MUMMY MUMSY...
I was not aware than Thomas Jefferson ever saw The OHIO...he sent people that far west (and farther)...but did he go there?  It's still a bit quaint to realize that the Ohio territory was once "The Western Reserve."

Well, I knew it would be a challenge, and it was.  Wonderful!

weird in between for me – I didn’t like doing this puzzle, but i respect it. I think it’s pretty well made and there are some excellent clues there (‘boundaries between areas with different amounts of coverage’) 

but i got stuck so many times after assembling some big chunks, and i never really got in the flow of things wholesale. i havent had to do so many ‘check puzzles’ in ages.
i’ll accept that for this friday as a good puzzle even though it wasnt my cup of tea

Nice Friday puzzle - typical tough workout for me, and had to look up a couple of things, but still really enjoyed it. And... my puzzle find today: A Wednesday from June 10, 2015 by Tracy Gray. One theme answer, as best I can represent it: MEGOROUND Y_R _R And one more: SPINNING WHE __________S_E ___________L_ And the others: ASTHEWTURNS D_O LR ROLLINGST S_O EN Here's that link: https://www.xwordinfo.com/Crossword?date=6/10/2015&h=48a .....

Great puzzle! Had a ton of open space for quite some time but finally made progress with Think Big and What a Year. Still, the eastern quadrant was a struggle. 

BTW , This is my first comment after 3,213 solves!
48D was easy for me, since I’m a GRANT accountant for a research institution.

I had to pause mid-puzzle and had “With whom one pools pounds for quarters” rattling around in my head while I took care of some household tasks. By the time an answer occurred to me, I couldn’t remember how many letters it was and had to run back praying for 8 because I was so incredibly tickled with the possibility of FLATMATE. That might be my favorite clue/answer combo after 1600+ NYT crosswords. Incredible wordplay and airtight logic once it clicks. Bonus points for using units of currency from two different countries, both of which have multiple meanings. I’m in awe.

From the interwebs:

Scientific Progress Goes "Boink" is the title of the sixth collected edition of Bill Watterson's newspaper comic strip Calvin and Hobbes.   

The phrase comes from a famous storyline in the strip where Calvin builds or uses pseudo-scientific cardboard-box inventions—most notably a duplicator—that backfire hilariously and result in chaos (such as creating multiple chaotic clones of himself).

When Calvin's absurd, half-baked gadgets malfunction, pop out a copy, or break down, they often make a cartoonish "boink" sound.

"Boink" is OK because of crossword license, but I thought "boing" a better fit for the clue.
For anyone questioning BOINK here’s proof direct from a Calvin and Hobbes title: https://mainpointbooks.com/book/9780836218787
Great Friday puzzle. Thanks, Katie Hoody. Masterful cluing.
Hooray - based on the difficulty of this puzzle, it's already Saturday!

Reading the stories of your uncle made me think of one of mine. Uncle Bob always had a smile, sang us spontaneous, silly songs and made up sweet, funny nicknames for everyone.

I loved visiting him and my aunt, they were such jolly people, so kind and loving, a welcome respite from the stressful disfunction of my immediate family.

I'm glad you had that positive, happy influence. Thank you to the Uncle Bobs and Tims for some wonderful memories.

Oh, and the puzzle was lovely, a challenging Friday, as it should be.

Thanks!

People who don’t know tennis lingo are at a disadvantage (or should I say “ad-out”?) in crosswords — WHiP vs WHUP was the last speck. 

I thought Maryjanes were the height of sophistication

One more puzzle find, somewhat inspired by our constructor's surname. Wondered about... HOWDYDOODY and... a Tuesday from November 3, 2020 by Amanda Chung and Karl Ni. Probably did that one but of course had completely forgotten it. Anyway... some theme answers (in addition to HOWDYDOODY): HUMPTYDUMPTY HANDYDANDY HUNKYDORY HEAVYDUTY Here's that link: https://www.xwordinfo.com/Crossword?date=11/3/2020&h=18a ...
What a great puzzle. My stubbornness in holding onto HORSYRACE added a little time but the idea will make me smile all day

So I avoided the OLDEN trap because the O looked impossible for 1A and the D looked impossible for the track event.  When THOSE finally came in, I found myself thinking "Really?!"  But I suppose that THOSE DAYS can't be present or future -- so I guess there's that.

The trap I did fall into was fIXES for "scraps".  It wasn't quite right, but it wasn't quite wrong either.  I never thought of NIXES -- which left me with Bobby ?ARIF.  Who he?  

Nor did I know BYNES.  But I didn't cheat on BYNES, nor on HARTE,  I did cheat on KYRA.  Leading me to ethics question #1:

Is it more honorable, when you know you'll need to cheat, to cheat on the shorter name rather than the longer name -- even if there's only a 1-letter difference?  I've always thought that it is more honorable.  And I always strive to be honorable when cheating:)

I struggled everywhere -- even when there weren't any names involved.  One instance: I wanted ACCEnt something-or-other for the ensemble piece ACCESSORY.  Once again, I didn't write it in because there's no 3-letter family member beginning with an N.

A WASP NEST of a Friday puzzle with really tough cluing throughout.  I guess I did have fun in a masochistic sort of way.  Did anyone find it easy?  I'll go check the blog now.
"Constructor Notes" were almost as much fun to read as the puzzle was to solve.  Cheers to Uncle Tim.
Thanks Katie and Uncle Tim. Fun fun fun!
No spoilers: The Midi was very clever today! Impressive!
Hey fam! Do any of you drink orange juice out of a cup? Asking for a friend.
Fun puzzle!
Now THIS is what I’m talking about! Wonderful and challenging Friday. 10/10.
Gorgeous puzzle today, many highlights. Loved FLATMATE in particular. The constructor notes make me want to be a better aunt. I'm not crying you are 🥹

A HORSE RACE is not a track event. Track events are running events with humans. Horse races are equine sports. The clue would be acceptable if it had a question mark at the end, but without one it is factually wrong and RELAY RACE makes the most sense.
That was awesome. Seemingly impossible at first but then...
fabulous friday puzzle, more please
This was superb, indeed. One of the best of the year. Bravo, Katie!!

This was a lovely puzzle! Great clues, and I loved the constructor's story about her Uncle Tim.
Instead of METRONOME to start, I had METERMAID. Had to work to undo that.

Feeling sheepish that USTA was the last answer I filled in. My husband made it to the USTA Men's Singles Finals (55+) in Orlando this year! But at least it gave me an excuse to brag. 

Katie Hoody, you are a bit of a rascal. It must run in the family!

Thank you Katie for a marvelous puzzle! 
But mostly thank you so much for uncle Tim’s words. It was just what I needed today.

That’s gonna be another no for me. Two days in a row, two pretty miserable puzzles.  Amanda who? Bobby who? Emma who? BOINK not BOINg? WHATAYEAR? What a clue… I don’t mean to be a stinker but puzzles like these really bring me down: puzzles where the rewarding,  enjoyable moments are overshadowed by the filler. Maybe next week.
Big fan of this puzzle but I don’t quite understand WHUP? I looked up the definition but it still feels like a more rough fit than the rest of the clever puzzle so I’m worried I’m missing something.

A bit of a tussle
With this crossword puzzle.


An honest 80 minutes, but never annoying.
Darling Edie let me (5) down.
Kicked my butt in all 4 quadrants and the middle. Toughie! But I got there, with more than the usual help from my English-teaching spouse. Fully 50% over average Friday time. Phew!!

Learn this one word:  polysemy.
